correctness.rationale: Stationary balance of the habitat-A masses, using the autonomous marginal pi, gives Mx=diag(v)pi with M=D−sQᵀ and D=diag(u+v). The killed-chain semigroup has mass bounded by exp(−t min_i r_i), so M is invertible for s≥0 and its determinant retains its positive sign at zero. Subtracting c pi leaves input diag(pi)(v−cr); the adjugate bounds the benchmark numerator degree by m−1, including the identically zero exception and the constant one-mode case. For the complete graph the rank-one correction divides the sum of partial fractions by 1−s sum_i 1/(r_i+ms)>0. After multiplying by the positive common product, evaluation at the m distinct poles proves the prescribed monic numerator identity. Scaling its coefficients about v_i=cr_i keeps both directional rates strictly positive and preserves every prescribed simple zero. Independently expanding the example M determinant gives 8+28s+21s² and its benchmark numerator 9(s−1)(s−4)/128; the mean of the three isolated A probabilities is 137/256. Uniform behavior frequencies are exact, not simulated.
residual_risks: The theorem does not extend here to transient probabilities, habitat-dependent switching, or higher habitat counts. The supplied finite checks do not prove the general result.

value.rationale: Separates an unchanged behavior marginal from stationary spatial use and identifies exactly how many threshold crossings m modes can support. Prescribing every crossing speed with positive rates goes beyond a rational upper bound or one counterexample to simple behavioral weighting. This is a concrete model-design and interpretation result, not evidence about field occupancies.
residual_risks: No robustness margin, inference guarantee or field calibration is supplied.
